outcome: Scheduled jobs can now actually use the tools and capabilities you granted them. A scheduled run that reaches a command its agent is host-granted (like the gog Google Sheets commands) now asks the host coordinator to authorize it instead of dead-ending — so the job does its work instead of stalling — while the settings denylist stays a hard, un-overridable boundary and the agent still can't self-grant (PERM-2 preserved; decision 0116). And a job that genuinely must pause now sends you ONE plain-language message ("This job paused because it couldn't use X. Needed: …") instead of three overlapping technical cards. Codex validated the root cause read-only; 8781 unit tests, verify.py, and a whole-branch autoreview all green. One cosmetic edge case deferred (D-0052).
